name: Radio Dial
shortDescription: A vintage tuner for live internet radio, with a glowing dial and VU meters.
description: A radio page built like a tuner: a brushed brass plate, a backlit frequency strip behind frosted glass, and a needle that springs from station to station while the lamp warms and glows brighter when a station locks. The station name burns in Nixie tubes, two VU needles and a spectrum glass move with the music (or with a breathing pulse when a stream does not allow it to be read), and tuning plays a short burst of static that fades as the stream comes in. Your presets sit on the dial; Find searches the Radio Browser directory by name, genre, or country and slides results in as paper index cards you can add to the dial or star. Favorites and the last station stay in your browser, with Export and Import. Arrow keys tune, space plays, and the phone's lock screen carries the station. Your agent asks which stations you listen to, any countries or genres to load, and walnut, bakelite, or black steel, then builds the page.
setup:
Ask the person, in one message: Which stations do you listen to (names or stream links)? Any countries or genres to load onto the dial? Walnut, bakelite, or black steel?

Then copy inputs.example.json from the app folder to radio-dial.inputs.json in the project folder and edit it: name for the panel, theme (walnut, bakelite, or black-steel), and presets, one per station with its name and an https stream url, plus homepage, country, about (the line under the station name), and logo if you have them. For a station named without a link, or a country or genre, look it up with https://de1.api.radio-browser.info/json/stations/search?name=KEXP&hidebroken=true&order=votes&reverse=true&limit=10 (or tag=jazz, or country=Japan) and use url_resolved from rows whose url_resolved starts with https://. Delete the _notes object if you like; it only explains the keys.

Run python3 <app folder>/scripts/run.py from the project folder. It writes out/radio-dial/, which any static file server can host.
